title: The Echo of Sector Nine
premise: Jonah Sandoval tends the last terraforming garden on a half-dead world, keeping alive a beacon whose original commission records have been erased. When a ship that officially never flew appears in orbit with an unknown name on its manifest, Jonah discovers the beacon is actually a dead-man's switch: proof of a massacre both fleets have spent decades burying, and the only thing keeping them from open war over the jump corridor. Hunted by agents from both sides who need him silenced or weaponized, Jonah gathers a ragtag crew of survivors and deserters — a found family forged in the wreckage of official history. In the end, he broadcasts the truth through the beacon during the jump window, sacrificing his own safe passage to hold the fleets apart with honesty instead of lies, and his new family chooses to stay behind with him to rebuild what the war would have burned.
about_author: Ulyana Nystrom is a former hydrology consultant who left Earth's coastal restoration projects to write about people tending impossible futures. She lives off-grid on a decommissioned research station in the North Atlantic, where she grows heirloom tomatoes under artificial suns.

chapters.title: The Garden for No One
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. On the terraforming station Meridian, Jonah tends seedlings meant for colonists two generations away and maintains Beacon Nine, a transmitter no record explains. His quiet routine cracks when a supply drone delivers a manifest listing a ship called Vespera — a vessel he knows was scrapped before it ever launched. Emotional beat: loneliness interrupted by the first mystery.

chapters.title: Manifest Ghost
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Digging into corrupted archives, Jonah finds the name on the manifest: Ilsa Reyes, listed as navigator of a flight that never happened. A fleet survey team arrives asking oddly specific questions about the beacon's power draw. Jonah lies for the first time in years. Emotional beat: paranoia taking root as the ordinary world curdles.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Reyes, alive and hiding in Meridian's lower decks. She reveals she faked her death after Sector Nine's evacuation, when both fleets fired on civilian transports and blamed each other. The beacon holds the sensor logs proving mutual guilt — and someone has finally come to erase it. Emotional beat: grief shared becomes the first bond.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Corridor
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Fleet envoys from the Concord and the Compact arrive simultaneously, each claiming jurisdiction over the jump window opening in nineteen days. Jonah realizes his lie about the beacon's status is now the only thing preventing either side from seizing it. He recruits station misfits — engineer Dov, medic Sefa, runaway pilot Kesh — to help him stall. Emotional beat: reluctant leadership; the found family begins to assemble.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: POV Kesh. The crew runs sabotage disguised as maintenance, feeding both fleets false telemetry while Ilsa recovers the logs from the beacon's sealed core. Kesh, who lost her family in the Sector Nine evacuation, confronts Ilsa about why she stayed hidden so long. Emotional beat: anger at survivors who survived too well; trust tested and partially repaired.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Dov. A Concord agent uncovers part of the deception and takes Sefa hostage, demanding the beacon's core. Dov must choose between handing over the logs' location or watching a friend die. They trade a decoy core, buying days but burning their cover. Emotional beat: the cost of resistance made personal; guilt and resolve entwined.

chapters.title: Everything We Buried
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. With four days left, Ilsa decrypts the full logs and finds her own voice on the evacuation channel — proof she warned command and was ordered to stand down. Both fleets send strike teams; the window for escape on a smuggler's ship closes in seventy-two hours. Emotional beat: confronting complicity; choosing truth over self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Lie That Holds
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Cornered, Jonah doubles down on the lie: he tells both fleets the beacon will broadcast mutual-guilt evidence automatically if tampered with — a bluff built on real code Ilsa wrote. The strike teams stall, each side afraid to move first. But the bluff requires someone physically at the beacon when the jump window opens. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose; Jonah accepts he may be the price.

chapters.title: Jump Window
chapters.summary: POV Jonah, climax. As both fleets mass in orbit, Jonah broadcasts the true logs live through Beacon Nine — not as blackmail, but as testimony, naming every ship lost in Sector Nine. Fleets freeze, crews refusing orders to fire while the dead are read aloud. The strike teams stand down rather than martyr him. Emotional beat: catharsis; justice achieved outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: The Echo
chapters.summary: POV Jonah, resolution. Investigations begin on both sides; the guilty are named, the corridor opened under joint stewardship. Offered passage home, Jonah's crew instead stays to finish the garden — planting it now for people who will actually come. Ilsa adds the Sector Nine dead to the memorial manifest. Emotional beat: grief transformed into cultivation; family chosen, future planted.
